 Order

The first accused in C.C.No.210 of 2003 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Koyilandi, has filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16 (1-A) (i) r/w Section 7(i) and 2(ia) (b) and (j)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 29 and Rule 5 of Appendix B, para A.16.06.10 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Koyilandi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 6.1.2003 at about 12.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 1 Kg of green gram dhal from the shop of the first accused.
The first accused was the salesman cum licencee of the said shop.
The second accused was the manufacturer of the food item.
After taking the samples as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.
Ext.P12 report of the public analyst would show that the sample contained synthetic food colour tartrazine under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and was therefore adulterated.
Thereafter, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory on the request of the accused.

As per Ext.P22 certificate of analysis,
the sample contained synthetic food colour tartrazine and was therefore adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P23 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 to DW6 were examined and Exts.D1 to D10 were marked for the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P22 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee)
and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P22 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Mashood vs Food Inspector on 18 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82612478/
2 Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

entities.text: Mashood vs Food Inspector on 18 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16 (1-A) (i) r/w Section 7(i) and 2(ia) (b) and (j) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 29 and Rule 5 of Appendix B, para A.16.06.10 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioner stands cancelled and he is set at liberty.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/18.01.2016.
